entities.summary: Denise Schmandt-Besserat is a French-American archaeologist and retired professor of art and archaeology of the ancient Near East. She spent much of her professional career as a professor at the University of Texas. She is best known for her work on the history and invention of writing. While her research is highly cited, it has been controversial among scholars. The controversies, as detailed below, concern the interpretation of early tokens, particularly the complex ones; however, the idea that writing emerged out of the counting, cataloging, management, and transactions of agricultural produce has been largely accepted.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Denise Schmandt-Besserat's work on the history and invention of writing has had a significant impact on our understanding of the emergence of writing systems in ancient civilizations. Her research has also sparked important discussions about the relationship between writing and agriculture.
